questions.q: Two tall pea plants produce a few dwarf offspring. Assuming simple Mendelian dominance of tallness, which parental cross best explains the result?
questions.explanation: A dwarf offspring must receive the recessive allele from both parents and therefore have genotype tt. Each tall parent must consequently carry a hidden recessive allele while still expressing the dominant tall phenotype. The only listed cross satisfying those conditions is Tt x Tt.

questions.q: A dihybrid F2 shows the classic phenotypic ratio 9:3:3:1. What is the strongest inference about the two gene pairs?
options: A) They show complete linkage and never recombine
B) Their alleles segregate independently, as expected for independently assorting genes
C) They are multiple alleles of the same gene
D) One gene completely suppresses the other
questions.answer: B) Their alleles segregate independently, as expected for independently assorting genes
questions.explanation: The Exemplar directly links the 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio with independent segregation of the two gene pairs. Such a ratio is the expected outcome when the combinations of alleles assort independently into gametes. Complete linkage or strong gene interaction would alter the classic Mendelian ratio.

questions.q: A test cross of a dihybrid gives four offspring classes in nearly equal numbers: 138 tall-red, 132 tall-white, 136 dwarf-red and 128 dwarf-white. Which parental interpretation best fits these data?
options: A) Both parents were homozygous dominant for both genes
B) The tall-red parent was homozygous dominant and the other parent was heterozygous
C) The tall-red parent was heterozygous for both genes and was crossed with a double-recessive tester
D) Both parents were double recessive
questions.answer: C) The tall-red parent was heterozygous for both genes and was crossed with a double-recessive tester
questions.explanation: The four phenotypic classes occur in approximately equal numbers, which is the hallmark of a 1:1:1:1 test-cross expectation for two independently assorting heterozygous gene pairs. The Exemplar provides essentially these four counts and asks for the parental genotypes. Therefore the tall-red parent must be heterozygous for both traits and the tester must be recessive for both.

questions.q: A child has blood group O, while the mother has blood group A and the father has blood group B. Which parental genotypes are required for this to be possible?
questions.explanation: Blood group O requires genotype ii, so the child must receive one i allele from each parent. A phenotypically A parent can supply i only if heterozygous IAi, and a phenotypically B parent can supply i only if heterozygous IBi. Hence both parents must be heterozygous as shown in option D.
